senses.gloss: A jester kept by a king or a noble household to entertain with jokes and songs.
examples: In the play, only the *fool* dares tell the king the truth.
The court *fool* wore a cap with bells on it.
Medieval kings kept *fools* to amuse their guests.

senses.gloss: The member of a jury who speaks for the group and reads out the verdict.
examples: The *foreman* stood up and read the verdict.
The judge asked the *foreman* whether the jury had reached a decision.
They elected a retired teacher as *foreman* on the first day.

senses.gloss: A place where a road or river divides into two branches, or one of those branches.
examples: Turn left at the *fork* in the road.
The trail splits at a *fork* about a mile in.
Both *forks* of the river meet again below the dam.

senses.gloss: The shape or outward appearance of something.
examples: A dark *form* moved behind the curtain.
The carving keeps the rough *form* of a bird.
We could barely make out the *forms* of the mountains in the fog.

senses.gloss: A type or variety of something.
examples: Swimming is the best *form* of exercise for her knees.
Cash is still an accepted *form* of payment here.
The disease takes several different *forms*.

senses.gloss: The level at which a person or team is performing at the moment.
examples: The team has been in great *form* since the break.
After his injury he struggled to get back to *form*.
The comedian was in fine *form* last night.

senses.gloss: Chance or luck seen as a force that decides what happens to people.
examples: By sheer good *fortune*, nobody was hurt.
*Fortune* seemed to be on our side that week.
He had the bad *fortune* to arrive in the middle of a blizzard.

senses.gloss: What is supposed to lie ahead for someone, as told by a person who claims to see the future.
examples: A woman at the fair offered to tell my *fortune*.
The *fortune* in my cookie said travel was coming.
She has her *fortune* read every New Year.

senses.gloss: In baseball, a ball hit outside the lines that mark fair territory.
senses.ru: фол-бол (мяч за пределами игровой зоны, бейсбол)
examples: He hit two *fouls* down the third-base line.
The umpire called it a *foul* by inches.
Every *foul* into the stands sent kids scrambling for the ball.

senses.gloss: A clever, crafty person who is hard to outwit.
examples: That old *fox* saw the trap coming a mile away.
Her grandfather was a sly *fox* in business.
You'll never outsmart him; he's a *fox*.

senses.gloss: The way a subject or question is presented, which shapes how people understand it.
examples: The *framing* of the question pushed people toward one answer.
Both papers reported the same facts with very different *framing*.
Changing the *framing* from 'cost' to 'investment' won over the board.

senses.gloss: A person who pretends to be something he or she is not.
examples: The so-called doctor turned out to be a *fraud*.
She called the whole panel a bunch of *frauds*.
He felt like a *fraud* on his first day of teaching.

senses.gloss: In the plural, extra features or comforts that are pleasant but not necessary.
examples: It's a cheap flight with no *frills*.
The apartment is plain and has none of the *frills* we saw downtown.
We cut the *frills* out of the budget first.

senses.gloss: A border of hanging threads or cords on a rug, a lampshade, or a piece of clothing.
examples: Her jacket had leather *fringe* along the sleeves.
The rug's *fringe* was starting to unravel.
Silk *fringe* hung from the edge of the lampshade.

senses.gloss: The outer edge of an area, or the part of a group farthest from the center.
examples: They live on the *fringe* of town, past the last stoplight.
The idea started on the *fringes* of the party and slowly moved to the center.
Deer feed along the *fringe* of the woods at dusk.

senses.gloss: The part or side of something that faces forward.
examples: There's a long scratch on the *front* of the car.
We sat at the *front* of the classroom.
The *front* of the building is all glass.

senses.gloss: The line along which two armies are fighting in a war.
examples: Her grandfather was wounded at the *front*.
Fresh troops were sent to the eastern *front*.
Letters from the *front* took weeks to arrive.

senses.gloss: A person or business used to hide an illegal or secret activity.
examples: The car wash was a *front* for a gambling ring.
Police say the charity was just a *front*.
Several *fronts* were set up to move the money.

senses.gloss: A low, gloomy mood that a person cannot easily shake off.
examples: He's been in a *funk* since he lost his job.
A long walk usually pulls me out of a *funk*.
The whole team fell into a *funk* after that loss.

senses.gloss: An enclosed chamber that produces intense heat for melting metal or making glass.
examples: The steel mill's *furnace* runs day and night.
Workers fed scrap iron into the *furnace*.
Glassblowers pull molten glass straight from the *furnace*.

senses.gloss: A deep line or wrinkle in the skin, especially on the forehead.
examples: Worry had cut deep *furrows* in his brow.
A *furrow* appeared between her eyebrows as she read the letter.
Years of sun and wind left *furrows* across his face.

senses.gloss: A cord or device that is lit or set to make a bomb or a firework go off.
examples: He lit the *fuse* and stepped back.
The *fuse* burned down in a few seconds.
The bomb squad cut the *fuses* on the device.

senses.gloss: A blending of two or more different things into a single one.
examples: The restaurant serves a *fusion* of Korean and Mexican food.
Their sound is a *fusion* of jazz and hip-hop.
The merger created a *fusion* of two very different company cultures.

senses.gloss: A piece of cloth or tape put over someone's mouth to keep them from speaking.
examples: The robbers tied her hands and put a *gag* in her mouth.
He worked the *gag* loose with his tongue.
Police found ropes and *gags* in the trunk of the car.

senses.gloss: The highest balcony of seats in a theater, where the cheapest tickets are.
examples: We could only afford seats in the *gallery*.
Applause came down from the *gallery*.
The *gallery* was packed with students.

senses.gloss: A set of pictures displayed together, especially on a website or a phone.
examples: Click through the *gallery* to see all the photos.
The paper posted a *gallery* of shots from the parade.
My phone's photo *gallery* is out of space.

senses.gloss: The kitchen on a ship or an airplane.
examples: The cook was busy in the *galley*.
Flight attendants stowed the carts in the *galley*.
The boat has a tiny *galley* with a two-burner stove.

senses.gloss: A long ancient ship driven by rows of oars.
examples: Roman *galleys* once patrolled these waters.
The museum has a model of a Greek *galley*.
Prisoners were sentenced to row in the *galleys*.

senses.gloss: Wild animals or birds hunted for sport or for food.
examples: The lodge serves venison and other *game*.
*Game* is scarce in these hills now.
He grew up hunting small *game* with his father.

senses.gloss: A particular line of business or activity, especially a competitive one.
examples: She's been in the restaurant *game* for twenty years.
He got out of the news *game* after the layoffs.
New to the real estate *game*, he made a few costly mistakes.

senses.gloss: A quick look at something.
examples: Take a *gander* at this photo.
Let me have a *gander* at the menu.
He stopped to take a *gander* at the car in the driveway.

senses.gloss: A space or opening between two things or in something solid.
examples: The dog squeezed through a *gap* in the fence.
Cold air came in through the *gap* under the door.
There were wide *gaps* between the boards on the porch.

senses.gloss: A large difference between two amounts, groups, or levels.
examples: The *gap* between rich and poor keeps growing.
There's still a pay *gap* between men and women in the field.
The team closed the *gap* to three points.

senses.gloss: A shop where cars are repaired and serviced.
examples: My car has been at the *garage* all week.
He runs a small *garage* out on Route 9.
Both *garages* in town quoted me the same price.

senses.gloss: The place in an airport where passengers wait and board a plane.
examples: Our flight leaves from *gate* 12.
They changed the *gate* twenty minutes before boarding.
We ran the whole length of the terminal to our *gate*.

senses.gloss: A standard measure of the thickness of wire or metal, or of the size of a shotgun barrel.
examples: Sheet metal comes in several *gauges*, from thin to heavy.
Use a heavier *gauge* of wire for the kitchen outlets.
Nurses pick a smaller *gauge* of needle for children.

senses.gloss: A fact or test used to judge how much of something there is.
examples: Turnout is a rough *gauge* of how people feel about the mayor.
Ticket sales are the best *gauge* of a show's success.
Early polls are a poor *gauge* of the final result.

senses.gloss: One of the settings of a vehicle's transmission that controls speed and power.
examples: Shift into a lower *gear* before the hill.
The truck was stuck in first *gear*.
My bike has twenty-one *gears*.

senses.gloss: The first small beginning of an idea or plan, from which it can grow.
examples: The novel started as the *germ* of an idea on a napkin.
There's the *germ* of a good plan in what you just said.
His notebooks are full of the *germs* of stories he never wrote.

senses.gloss: Something done to show a feeling or an intention toward other people.
examples: Sending flowers was a nice *gesture*.
The company offered refunds as a *gesture* of goodwill.
Small *gestures* like that mean a lot to patients.

senses.gloss: An escape, especially one made by criminals right after a crime.
examples: The robbers made their *getaway* in a stolen van.
A witness wrote down the *getaway* car's plate number.
Police blocked every road to cut off their *getaway*.

senses.gloss: A natural ability to do something well.
examples: She has a *gift* for languages.
His *gift* for making people laugh got him the job.
Not everyone is born with musical *gifts*.

senses.gloss: A job, especially a temporary or freelance one.
examples: She picked up a *gig* driving for a delivery app.
He landed a *gig* writing copy for a startup.
A lot of people work two or three *gigs* to get by.

senses.gloss: One of the thin ribs on the underside of a mushroom cap.
examples: The *gills* under the cap were dark brown.
You can identify many mushrooms by the color of their *gills*.
Brush the dirt off the cap without tearing the *gills*.

senses.gloss: A glassy coating baked onto pottery to seal and decorate it.
examples: The bowl has a deep blue *glaze*.
She mixes her own *glazes* in the studio.
The *glaze* cracked in the kiln.
